newsitem.title: CHINA: Lafarge to double China investment by 200.
newsitem.headline: Lafarge to double China investment by 200.

text.p: Lafarge Group expects to double its China investments to reach $200 million in the next two to three years to meet growing demand for building materials, chairman Bertrand Collomb said on Thursday.

He said the French company was looking at opportunities stemming from Chinese government efforts to upgrade domestic cement production as well as the growing demand for cement, concrete and other materials due to rapid economic development.
"There is potential in this country which is considerable," he told Reuters in an interview.
"There is a need for concrete of better quality and for modern technology," he said.
Company officials quoted Chinese statistics as showing total demand for cement at 450 million tonnes this year. Demand is expected to rise to 600 million tonnes annually between 2005 and 2010.
Collomb estimated demand for cement in the United States was less than 100 million tonnes a year while demand in France was less than 20 million tonnes.
Many of China's cement makers are small and inefficient. As much as 80 percent of China's existing cement production currently uses outdated technology such as vertical kilns, he said.

The Chinese government was eager to promote the use of more efficient technology, particularly if it reduced pollution. That made China more receptive to foreign participation in the domestic market, Collomb said.
Lafarge already has three joint ventures in China with total investments of $200 million from all partners involved.

Earlier on Thursday, Lafarge announced a joint venture it controls on the outskirts of Beijing would invest another $75 million to expand cement production capacity to one million tonnes a year from 230,000 tonnes currently.
Lafarge also has a controlling interest in a ready-mix concrete plant in Beijing and a plasterboard plant that will begin production in Shanghai next year.
